decisions.rationale: In the title, 'ovarian cancer' functions as a noun modifier of 'cell lines' (ovarian cancer cell lines), so it is a disease mention used to modify another concept.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 3: Annotate disease mentions that are used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'ovarian cancers' is a plural that refers to a family of multiple specific cancers of the ovary rather than one defined disease, and it is the head of the phrase 'derived from human ovarian cancers'.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 1: Disease Class versus Specific Disease

decisions.rationale: 'ovarian tumor' modifies 'cell lines' in 'ovarian tumor cell lines' and is used as a modifier for another noun phrase.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 3: Annotate disease mentions that are used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'serous cystadenocarcinoma' names one specific cancer type with a single definition and no further categorization, as used for cell line 2774.
'ovarian tumors' is used as a general plural referring to the family of tumors arising in the ovary, which covers multiple specific diseases.
'tumor' modifies 'tissue' in 'bulk tumor tissue' and is used as a modifier; 'tumor' is retained as a disease term under the general-terms rule.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 3: Modifiers; What NOT to Annotate 4: general terms (cancer and tumor are retained)

decisions.rationale: 'ovarian tumor' is used as a head noun referring generically to an ovarian tumor, which is a category covering multiple tumor types rather than one specific definition.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 1: Disease Class; Examples 11 (grey-area terms)

decisions.rationale: 'hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer' is a single named hereditary disease (HNPCC) with one specific definition, so the full phrase is the minimum necessary span.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 1: Specific Disease; Annotation Guidelines 5: minimum necessary span

decisions.rationale: 'tumorigenesis' refers to a biological process rather than a disease, so it is excluded.
